questions.question: Which international standard specifies the determination of shrinkage temperature of leather up to 100 °C, and what physical phenomenon does it measure?

answers.a: ISO 5402; mechanical flex cracking under cyclic bending stress
answers.b: ISO 3380 (IUP 16); hydrothermal denaturation and longitudinal contraction of collagen fibers under controlled aqueous heating
answers.c: ISO 2420; apparent bulk density and porosity of tanned hides
answers.d: ISO 11640; color transfer fastness to reciprocal dry and wet crocking

questions.question: At the macromolecular level, what structural transition in collagen triggers the macroscopic hydrothermal shrinkage of leather?

answers.a: Cleavage of primary covalent peptide bonds along the polypeptide backbone into single amino acids
answers.b: Cooperative rupture of interchain hydrogen bonds causing the rigid triple helix of tropocollagen to collapse into a random coil gelatin conformation
answers.c: Sublimation of crystalline water clusters into steam cavities within the grain pores
answers.d: Cross-linking of lipid fatliquors with basic chromium salts

questions.question: What is the typical hydrothermal shrinkage temperature (Ts) range of raw, untanned collagen or pickled pelt in water?
Why does standard chrome-tanned leather (Wet Blue) exhibit a hydrothermal shrinkage temperature typically exceeding 100 °C?

answers.a: Chromium ions form an impervious glassy coating on the exterior surface
answers.b: Polynuclear Chromium(III) complexes form coordinate covalent cross-links with carboxyl groups of aspartic and glutamic acid residues via olation and oxolation bridges
answers.c: Chromium salts eliminate all water molecules, converting collagen into crystalline graphite
answers.d: Chromium reduces the molecular weight of collagen so it can no longer coil

questions.question: In accordance with ISO 3380, what are the prescribed dimensions for the test specimen strip cut from the conditioned leather?
What standardized heating rate (dT/dt) is strictly specified in ISO 3380 during the critical thermal approach to the shrinkage temperature?
Why is continuous, gentle magnetic stirring mandatory throughout the shrinkage temperature determination?

answers.a: To dissolve the tanning chemicals out of the specimen into the bath
answers.b: To eliminate thermal stratification and boundary-layer temperature gradients around the specimen and thermometer bulb
answers.c: To mechanically stretch the leather fibers until they reach yield point
answers.d: To introduce dissolved oxygen to accelerate collagen thermal oxidation

questions.question: What is the primary function of the lightweight counterweight (approx. 3.0 g / 0.03 N) suspended over the low-friction pulley?

answers.a: To calibrate the electrical conductivity of the immersion fluid
answers.b: To maintain slight positive tension keeping the wet strip taut without inducing mechanical creep or elongation
answers.c: To measure the Archimedean buoyant force of the leather
answers.d: To tear the specimen once the collagen bonds begin to soften

questions.question: Which repeating tripeptide amino acid sequence forms the primary structural motif of collagen alpha-chains?

answers.a: (Gly-X-Y)n, where X is commonly proline and Y is commonly hydroxyproline
answers.b: (Ala-Leu-Val)n, where Valine occupies every second residue

questions.question: Why does vegetable-tanned leather typically display a shrinkage temperature between 75 °C and 85 °C, lower than that of chrome-tanned leather?

answers.a: Vegetable tannins destroy the polypeptide chains rather than preserving them
answers.b: Vegetable polyphenolic tannins primarily stabilize collagen through multi-point hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions rather than thermally robust covalent coordination bonds
answers.c: Vegetable tannins are volatile and evaporate completely at 70 °C
answers.d: Vegetable tanning only reacts with the epidermis layer of the hide
